items.title: 61521_David Albert Francis oral history interview
items.q: So he said, 'Would you like to join my group?', so I told him yes

ctx.x: So I went -- there was a club on 116th Street called the Masopeka, and I went there; that was where I first heard Lips Page and Roy Eldridge; they had a jam session there, and I sat in there.

So it happened there was a saxophone player was also there by the name of Tab Smith. Tab Smith heard me, and so he asked me if I was working with some band around town, and I said, "No, I'm not -- I just came here from Florida" -- and I had a southern accent you could cut with a knife at that time, and so he said, "Well, how long have you been in town?"

And I said, 'Well, I just got here -- I only been here like 2 days.' So he said, 'Would you like to join my group?', so I told him yes, and he said, 'Well, can you start with me Sunday night?' I said, 'Yeah' -- and I didn't ask how much the job paid or nothing.

items.title: Panama Francis interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 1, 1995
items.q: A native of Miami, David played his first engagements with the Florida Collegians and in New York with Tab Smith.

ctx.x: Drummer David “Panama” Francis has been performing professionally since the 1930’s. A native of Miami, David played his first engagements with the Florida Collegians and in New York with Tab Smith. Later gigs with Billy Hicks, Roy Eldridge, Lucky Millinder and Cab Calloway made him a familiar and sought-after drummer for both recordings and live shows.
